chapters.title: A canal that carries everything except boats
chapters.verdict: Built 1806-1882 to carry salt, firewood and dried fish into Madras, the Buckingham Canal today is Chennai's flood carrier, sewage conduit, and the spine of the city's eastern water system: 74.5 km, measured here end to end, two hundred metres at a time.

chapters.title: The industrial mouth
chapters.verdict: On paper, no factory discharges to the canal any more. This week, the fish died anyway.

chapters.title: The city squeeze
chapters.verdict: Survey records give the canal up to 143 metres through the city. We measured 9 at the narrowest. The railway that did it is exempt from the court order that would undo it.

reaches.name: Basin Bridge to the Cooum junction

chapters.title: The marsh's only drain
chapters.verdict: Everything South Chennai drains passes through one 2.8 km channel into this canal. In 2026 it was squeezed to under 10 metres, the flamingos did not come, and the hyacinth bloom that followed is visible from orbit.

chapters.title: The living estuary
chapters.verdict: Where the tide still reaches, the canal still lives: 126 bird species, working fishers, a boat house - behind a sand bar that closes seven months a year.

reaches.name: Muttukadu backwater and the Kovalam inlet

chapters.title: The forgotten ribbon
chapters.verdict: South of Kovalam the canal is intact and abandoned at once: eleven structure-free kilometres running green with vegetation, past a wetland the city now wants as a reservoir.

chapters.title: The paper canal
chapters.verdict: Seventeen years of sanctions, orders and tenders; a High Court clock that ran out; four custodians and no funded mandate. The canal's paperwork is a river of its own.

chapters.title: What a pilot would measure
chapters.verdict: The state's monitoring of this canal is thinner than its plans for it: the best monthly series died in 2023, no gauge sits on the canal, and this week's fish kill awaits a lab result. This page is the baseline. A pilot keeps it alive.
